findings.title: Whole-buffer JSON decoding loses the actual reader final status on multi-request output
findings.trigger: Any otherwise qualified invocation that reaches at least one request status followed by a final reader result; every successful acquisition necessarily has archive and listing progress lines plus a final line.
findings.actual_path: Conserved reader.get line92 prints a complete JSON status per request. acquire_normal304/339 invokes archive then listing; up to3 artifact calls follow. main597 then prints final ACQUISITION_COMPLETE JSON;599/601 similarly print STOP_UNKNOWN after prior request output. The wrapper captures all stdout and applies json.loads(output) at79, which only accepts one JSON document. Multiple producer documents cause ExtraData, caught by82; safe remainsNone and is persisted in83.
findings.consequence: Intended retained closed final status and logical_GETs are systematically absent for successful multi-request acquisition and for post-request stops. The raw stdout is correctly not persisted, and no later wrapper code reparses the final line or selects that final record. This is a reachable producer/consumer interface defect before the bounded one-shot acquisition.
findings.downstream_check: Native transport receipts still retain actual inner native_exit/category/EOF/join/closure. The wrapper reports ROOT_READER_INVOCATION_RETURNED rather than PASS; safeNone does not invent success. No capture bypass, raw-content leak, wrong-target request or unsafe acquisition acceptance is alleged. Existing source-only reader review14294 remains valid; it did not qualify this then-unexamined wrapper.
findings.required_correction: Preserve frozen v1 and apply minimal versioned final-record selection compatible with actual reader JSON-lines output, retaining only allowed closed final status/int GET count. Keep exact native/admission/once/retention behavior. Source-bound pure RAM controls should cover archive+listing(+artifacts) progress then COMPLETE, progress then STOP_UNKNOWN, one-line PRE_GET_REFUSED and malformed/partial/nonqualifying final data, with no actual functions/transport/acquisition by reviewer.
